name: Sihor
overview: Sihor, also called Shihor, is identified in Scripture as a river of Egypt, often understood to be the Nile River. The references in Joshua 13:3 and 1 Chronicles 13:5 mark it as a geographical boundary significant to Israel’s history, from which David gathered the people to bring the ark of God. Isaiah 23:3 highlights the prosperity associated with the waters of Sihor, describing it as a source of abundance and a center of commerce. Jeremiah 2:18 uses the imagery of drinking the waters of Sihor to question reliance on Egypt, underscoring its symbolic and practical importance in biblical narrative.
